newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian paranormals see another gloomy year.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian paranormals see another gloomy year.

text.p: Indonesian paranormals have predicted another gloomy year for their country in 1997 in an annual survey published by the Jakarta Post newspaper on Sunday.

The same group of seers last year forecast with a degree of accuracy that the political temperature would soar and corruption, manipulation and collusion would run even more rampant. They also predicted increased natural disasters.
"The year of 1997 will not be better than 1996. Wicked people will be more vicious. Those in power will be more arrogant and mean," promiment soothsayer Ki Ageng Selo was quoted as saying.

Hundreds died in a ferry sinking in Aceh in February and the nation was shaken by the death of the President Suharto's wife in April. Earthquakes struck remote provinces throughout the year, while floods in the capital killed more than 20 people.

There were major riots in two cities in Irian Jaya and hostage taking incidents, political discontent continued to rumble in East Timor and there were outbreaks of ethnic and religious violence in east and west Java.
People also died in protests in Sulawesi and Jakarta.
Predictions of soothsayers are watched closely by a large number of Indonesians, including some in high positions, who still hold to many superstious values despite rapid modernisation.

In a recent scandal, for example, a local official from Yogyakarta was found to have paid more than $400,000 to a seer, said to be acting as an intermediary, so he could be reappointed for another term.

Politics in Indonesia this year was dominated by the government-backed split in the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) when its leader Megawati Sukarnoputri was ousted by rival Surjadi in a party congress in Medan in June.

Megawati's supporters were violently evicted by police from PDI headquarters on July 27 in an act which triggered widespread rioting in the capital, the like of which had not been seen for more than 20 years. Five people died on that day.
Ki Gendeng Pamungkas, who claims to have learned voodoo in Nigeria and Haiti and to have killed hundreds of people with black magic, predicted a recurrence of such an event.
"A bloody riot such as the one on July 27 this year might happen again in 1997," he was quoted as saying.
Pyschic Mama Terate was less specific, saying: "The year 1997 will be an unfavourable year for everybody on this planet."
Putri Wong Kam Fu said 1997 was not only the year of the Ox, but the Fire Ox, so there would be a tendency for many things to be turned upside down. "The situation will be uncertain and chaotic."
Selo had predicted last year that advocates of democracy, including non-government organisations and students, would forge an alliance between June and August.

"The situation will be hot, but it will be under control. The election will run smoothly. The PDI, now torn by internal conflict, will see a brighter future. There will be a reconciliation between its chairman Surjadi and Megawati in April," he was quoted as saying.
Permadi Satriowiwoho, convicted in 1995 for blasphemy after giving a speech, said 1997 would be an unpredictable year because it was the climax of the "crazy era" in the Javanese cycle.

"There will be more natural disasters like earthquakes, typhoons, volcanic eruptions and there will be more riots, violence, murders and terrorism involving not only civilians but armed forces members and government officials," he said.
